_comment: Valinor Smart Cuff GUI update manifest. This feed accepts only
v3.2.* releases and is intentionally separate from version.json.
The installed client needs no GitHub credential and fails silently offline.
notes:
Smart Cuff Valinor v3.2.74

SysID now measures HIGH, uses LOW acquisition during natural exposure recovery, waits only for any remaining verified venting, then measures MID. Pressure-matched discovery and three independent response checks per band retain full settling for active measurements. Fine backfill and the final adjacent-duty crossing pass determine measured boundaries even when acquisition revisits duties out of order. Final quality, PID apply, snapshot and offline trust gates recompute the evidence; incomplete or rejected measurements cannot replace known-good tuning.

The result view distinguishes completed acquisition from accepted tuning and reports independent errors, useful LOW acquisition time, remaining vented wait and the original rejection reason. The unchanged firmware exposure limit, host probe margin and fresh continuous pump-off/vented completion gate remain enforced.

Valinor retains its 3 mmHg/s SysID reference, Max80 through Max220 menu, single-protocol gauge operation and GUI/standalone parity. Firmware rev27v-gauge-35 is unchanged from its protected-flashed and soaked profile.

Final frozen-source validation: Valinor 13/13 offline gates, 1205 tests passed and 5 skipped; focused final regression 61 passed. Default 13/13 gates, 1356 passed and 6 skipped. Both layout audits CLEAN; actual Qt smoke tests caught no exceptions.

The common SysID method was bench-tested on Default larger-cuff run117: independent HIGH/MID/LOW maximum rate errors 0.366/0.205/0.332 mmHg/s and offline trust PASS. Useful LOW work cleared the measured exposure bound, leaving 2.110 seconds of additional venting. Parsed Arduino sequence delivery was 100.0%, with zero missing sequence IDs; 340,200 native NI samples had zero timestamp backtracks. One malformed serial row remains retained separately. This is shared-method evidence, not a new Valinor hardware validation or tuning adoption.

Historical small-cuff runs94-96 supplied usable HIGH replay windows but ended before MID/LOW and have no independent held-out checks. Different pressures, actuator approach histories and missing exact worker-window records prevent cross-cuff tuning-transfer validation. Run117 general recording calibration review remains FAIL; separate bounded native sealed plateaus gave identity MAE 0.521 mmHg and p95 1.308 mmHg without changing calibration or NI acquisition time. Neither cuff transfer nor 1000-device manufacturing yield is qualified.

This complete branch-specific application retains app-local Python and Arduino tooling, verified automatic delivery and offline startup. Calibration history and accepted snapshots remain protected. Fleet profiles require individual Issues-only enrollment, maintainer review and verified application release distribution. No shared publishing credential or workstation flash receipt is shipped.

Reference pairing audit: the general recording checker carried forward NI values with median age 17.274 s, p95 28.304 s and maximum 28.985 s on run117. Native NI timestamps were retained; no clock or calibration change was made. This run does not establish live display freshness under concurrent bench capture/build load.

Native read-delay audit under concurrent bench capture/build load also measured median 17.207 s, p95 28.287 s and maximum 28.966 s. This is acquisition delivery latency despite monotonic timestamps; live freshness under that load is unresolved, not certified by the SysID trust result.
